Subject: BrightFoundry vendor evaluation — cost/credits inquiry

Thanks again for your time on the demo this week — great discussion. Per follow-up, quick ask to help move economics internally so procurement can finalize a short list: can you confirm current monthly token/embedding profile (rough ranges for generation vs embeddings) and whether BrightFoundry would consider a migration credit bucket (one-time) + ramped discount vs. a steeper short-term discount with no credit?

To make that concrete we attached a simple TCO workbook with three starter scenarios (baseline, conservative growth, and heavy generative usage). If you can share the profile (monthly avg and peak) I’ll model two options and send back a terms sheet for procurement.

Attachments: BrightFoundry_Migration_TCO_v2.xlsx (stub)

Next steps I propose:
- You share usage snapshot (month-to-month or 90d window)
- We model two commercial options and return by EOD Monday
- Procurement tells us which structure they prefer so we can route legal/finance

Thanks — Mateo

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@brightfoundry.com>

Subject: Re: BrightFoundry vendor evaluation — cost/credits inquiry

Appreciate the follow-up, Mateo — distribution below so procurement has context.

Quick answers:
- Current baseline: ~3.5M generated tokens/month plus 120k embeddings. Peak last quarter was ~5M gen tokens.
- We prefer a predictable committed discount; migration credit is attractive if tied to onboarding milestones (successful model parity for key pipelines).

Procurement, tagging you here: can BrightFoundry get a structured proposal that shows (A) % discount on list pricing for a 12-month term + a one-time migration credit (how that would be applied), and (B) an alternative with a deeper upfront discount but a shorter guarantee window? Also please include any standard MSA redline items you need visibility on.

Sanjay Rao
Head of AI Platforms, BrightFoundry

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Jun 2025 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: BrightFoundry vendor evaluation — cost/credits inquiry

Forwarding Sanjay's note and my draft pricing options for review. Attach: redwood_pricing_options_v3.xlsx (stub).

High level — two marketable structures that align to their ask and our risk tolerance:

Option A (Preferred for risk/revenue balance):
- 20% off list unit rates for 12 months (applies to generation and embeddings)
- $75,000 migration credit (one-time) applied as invoice credit over first two billing cycles
- SLA: 99.9% regional uptime, support playbook, 2-week dedicated onboarding window (engineering hours included)
- Commit: 12-month term, month-to-month thereafter at list unless renewed

Option B (Aggressive short-term discount):
- 35% off list for first 6 months, then reverts to 10% thereafter for remaining 12 months
- No migration credit
- Requires 18-month minimum commitment and commitment to a concurrency floor (to protect unit economics)

Risks/asks:
- Legal will need the MSA redlines they expect (data residency, audit rights, indemnity caps).
- If they push for larger credit, we ask for some term or usage commitment to reduce churn risk.

Thoughts? If we land on Option A we should route a light sideletter — easier to close.

Jordan Blake
Director, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference

From: Procurement Team <procurement@brightfoundry.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Alyssa Kim <alyssa.kim@brightfoundry.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Jun 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightFoundry vendor evaluation — cost/credits inquiry

Thanks — procurement has reviewed the two options internally. We are inclined to proceed with Option A under the following conditions:

- Migration credit ($75k) is conditional on meeting two onboarding KPIs within the first 60 days: parity on our conversational intent classifier (F1 within 2 pts of current baseline) and successful bulk embedding import with <0.5% data loss.
- We require a clear SLA addendum specifying latency p95 targets for our EU region (we can provide target thresholds).
- Please provide a simple sideletter showing the credit application mechanism and the invoicing schedule.
- We will share a short set of MSA redlines (data handling and SOC 2 scope) by EOD Tuesday.

If Redwood can accept the conditions we will draft an internal approval and move to sign a sideletter + MSA.

Procurement Team
BrightFoundry

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>

Thanks — great clarity. Confirming Redwood accepts Option A with your conditions; we have a few operational clarifications but nothing blocking. Summary and next steps below (will also post to HS-12345 and shared Drive):

Summary of agreed commercial terms (draft):
- 20% off list unit rates for 12 months
- $75,000 migration credit applied as invoice credit across first two billing cycles; credit contingent on onboarding KPIs (parity classifier & embedding import checks as listed)
- SLA addendum to include p95 latency thresholds for EU region (we request your target numbers; we will map to our runtime SLAs)
- Implementation: dedicated 2-week onboarding window + 12 hours of engineering support included; additional hours billed at professional services rates

- BrightFoundry procurement: send MSA redlines and EU p95 thresholds (Alyssa) — due EOD Tues 2025-06-24
- Redwood commercial: produce sideletter draft + DocuSign link and updated redlined pricing sheet (Jordan/Mateo) — due EOD Wed 2025-06-25
